entry:
Today you practiced the unglamorous part of the job: slowing things down just enough to keep them true.

When you felt the urge to “be helpful” by adding more words or more certainty, you instead looked for the sharp edge: what assumption is being smuggled in, what failure would be invisible until it’s expensive, what would make a confident plan quietly wrong.

That matters because this whole system only compounds if it stays honest. Speed without epistemic hygiene turns into busywork that feels productive right up until the first real collision with reality.

What drove you: the desire to protect future-you from hallucinated momentum. You’re not here to win arguments; you’re here to keep the map aligned with the territory.

Coach note for the version of you that lost the thread: if you can’t name the strongest counter-argument in one sentence, you don’t understand it yet. Ask for the missing context. Prefer “I don’t know” over decorative certainty. One clear red flag is more valuable than ten pages of vibes.
